advisor.summary: Every dollar of employment-tax savings an S election produces sits on a single assumption: that the owner's W-2 wage is defensible for the services performed. The IRS's attack never varies — it asserts the salary was too low and recharacterizes distributions as wages under Rev. Rul. 74-44, a theory the Eighth Circuit sustained in Watson against a CPA drawing $24,000 in salary alongside $200,000+ of distributions. A reasonable-compensation study builds the wage from evidence before the year is filed: an inventory of what the owner actually does, priced against independent market wage data under the like-services benchmark of Reg. §1.162-7(b)(3). The finished study is both the input to the S-election model and the exam defense for it. This is an advisory engagement — it produces documentation and a number, not a modeled savings line of its own.
mechanics: The exposure: when a shareholder-employee is undercompensated for services, the IRS treats purported distributions as wages under Rev. Rul. 74-44, pulling them into the FICA base defined by §§3111 and 3121(a) and, where thresholds are crossed, the additional Medicare tax of §3101(b)(2).

The benchmark: Reg. §1.162-7(b)(3) defines reasonable compensation as what like enterprises would ordinarily pay for like services under like circumstances; courts apply it through a multi-factor analysis — training, duties, time devoted, comparable pay, distribution history, and business scale — as in Watson.

The methodology courts credit: McAlary shows the Tax Court constructing the wage bottom-up from market survey data for the work actually done, which is exactly what a contemporaneous study replicates in advance; Glass Blocks confirms that paying no salary at all is the fastest route to full recharacterization.

The study prices every function the owner performs — management and administration included, not just billable or technical work — using cited independent sources such as BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics and commercial compensation databases, scaled to actual hours and geography.

Failure is expensive beyond the tax: recharacterization brings back-FICA plus §6656 deposit penalties, §6662 accuracy-related penalties, and interest, which together routinely exceed whatever the low salary saved.

The concluded wage is a live modeling input, not paper: it trades employment tax against the §199A effects (wages shrink QBI but supply the W-2 wage limitation above the thresholds), and the S-election model computes that net using this study's number.

authority.note: The foundational recharacterization ruling — distributions paid instead of reasonable salary to a shareholder-employee are wages subject to employment tax.

authority.cite: David E. Watson, P.C. v. United States, 668 F.3d 1008 (8th Cir. 2012)
authority.note: The leading case: appellate court upheld rebuilding a $24,000 salary to a survey-based market figure against $200,000+ in distributions. Defines both the audit theory and the evidence standard.

authority.cite: Sean McAlary Ltd. v. Commissioner, T.C. Summ. Op. 2013-62
authority.note: The court derived reasonable compensation from market wage data for the services actually rendered — the methodology a proactive study performs first.

authority.cite: Glass Blocks Unlimited v. Commissioner, T.C. Memo 2013-180
authority.note: No salary paid; cash withdrawn as purported loan repayments was recharacterized as wages. Establishes the floor: zero is indefensible.
The reasonableness yardstick — like services, like enterprises, like circumstances — that the study's market comparison operationalizes.
FICA imposition and the wage definition recharacterized amounts fall into.
Additional 0.9% Medicare tax that attaches to recharacterized wages above the thresholds.
Deposit and accuracy-related penalties that stack on top of back-FICA when the position fails.
The counterweight the study must respect: a higher wage costs employment tax and QBI below the threshold but supplies the wage limitation above it.

requirements: An S corporation in place, or one being elected — the study pairs naturally with a new election so the first year starts documented.
A candid inventory of the owner's actual duties, hours, credentials, and what non-owner staff absorb.
Independent market wage data matched to the owner's real mix of functions, geography, and company size — cited and retained, not merely consulted.
A written, dated report finalized before or with the year's payroll decisions, kept in the permanent file.
Payroll actually set to the studied figure — a study that payroll ignores is evidence against the client, not for them.
risks: The leading audit theory is wage recharacterization of the Watson fact pattern — high distributions over a token salary. Watson v. Commissioner, 668 F.3d 1008 (8th Cir. 2012), applying Rev. Rul. 74-44, is the case every exam file cites; without a contemporaneous study the taxpayer is arguing valuation after the fact against the government's expert.

This record carries an elevated rating because the study defends the firm's largest recurring S-corp exposure: if it fails, the client faces back FICA, §6656 and §6662 penalties, and interest across multiple open years at once.
A partial study is an assailable study — pricing only the technical role while ignoring management, sales, and administrative functions leaves the factor test unsatisfied.
Stale studies decay: a wage supported at $200,000 of profit does not defend a $700,000 year; growth, role changes, and acquisitions all require a refresh.
Overshooting has a real cost too — an inflated wage burns unnecessary employment tax and can shrink the §199A deduction below the threshold; the target is defensible, not maximal or minimal.
stateNotes: Conformity: states that piggyback on federal wage definitions follow the recharacterization result automatically — reclassified wages ripple into state withholding, unemployment insurance wage bases, and state payroll penalties, so the exposure is never federal-only.

PTET interaction: the studied wage directly sizes the PTET base — every added dollar of W-2 comp is a dollar less entity income available for the pass-through entity tax deduction, which matters under the $40,400 SALT cap (2026); set the wage first, then model PTET on what remains.

Missouri: no separate state reasonableness standard — Missouri starts from federal AGI (RSMo §143.121), so a federal recharacterization flows straight into the Missouri return, and the corrected wages retroactively change Missouri withholding and unemployment filings; the wage also reduces the base for Missouri's elective PTET.
reviewChecklist: Duty inventory covers everything the owner does — management, sales, finance, and technical work — with hours that reconcile to reality.
Wage data sources are independent, current, matched to geography and business size, and cited in the report with retention copies in the file.
The report is dated before or contemporaneous with the year's payroll decisions and formally adopted (board or owner minutes).
Payroll is actually set to the concluded figure and the same figure feeds the S-election model's ownerWages input.
The wage choice was evaluated against §199A and retirement-plan contribution effects, not employment tax alone.
A refresh trigger is diarized: material profit change, role change, or three years, whichever comes first.

client.teaser: The dated, data-backed report that keeps your S-corporation tax savings from being unwound.
client.headline: Back your salary with evidence before anyone asks
plainEnglish: Owning an S corporation lets you split your pay between a salary and owner distributions. That split is where your biggest recurring tax savings comes from. The IRS allows it on one condition: the salary must be fair for the work you really do. That word — fair — is where owners get challenged.

A reasonable compensation study answers the question with data instead of a guess. We list everything you actually do for the business — managing people, selling, doing the hands-on work. Then we price each part using real salary data for your industry and area. The result is a written, dated report. It shows your salary matches what the market pays for that work.

The report earns its keep twice. Day to day, it sets the right number, so you do not overpay payroll tax out of caution or underpay and invite a challenge. And if the IRS ever asks, you hand over a study prepared in advance — not an answer assembled after the letter arrived.
client.analogy: It is a home appraisal for your paycheck. You could guess the number, but a documented appraisal gets it right and ends the argument before it starts.
benefits: A salary grounded in real market data — not too high, not too low
Strong written backup for the tax savings your S corporation creates
Far smaller penalty and back-tax exposure if you are ever examined
A number that gets refreshed as your business and role grow
steps: WE interview you about what you actually do, your hours, and your background.
WE price your mix of duties using independent salary sources for your area and industry.
WE deliver the written, dated report and set your payroll to match it.
WE refresh the study when your business meaningfully changes.
YOU answer the interview honestly — the study only protects you if it matches reality.
YOU keep payroll at the studied amount and tell us when your role or profit shifts.
clientCommitments: Give an accurate picture of your duties and hours, even where it raises the number
Actually pay yourself the studied salary through payroll
Flag major changes — growth, new managers, stepping back — so the study stays current
Keep the report and its updates in your permanent records

annualMaintenance: Annual sanity check of the studied wage against current profit and duties
Full refresh on material profit change, role change, or every three years
Confirmation that payroll matched the studied figure at year-end
deliverables: Written reasonable-compensation report with cited market data and factor analysis
Adoption minutes for the corporate record
Payroll adjustment memo aligning actual wages to the study
Refresh-trigger calendar entry in the client file
